transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-22
Time: 10:00am PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Samantha Green (MapleHealth CTO), Luis Ramirez (ML Eng), Aisha Khan (Product)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan with Redwood, this is Ravi on the eng side. we're gonna run through our model catalog demo, show how to pick open models, look at benchmarks and a compatibility matrix. um, any quick intro from you folks?
[00:12] Samantha: yeah thanks, Samantha here. we're evaluating inference options for our clinical assistant feature, latency target is sub-200ms for short prompts but cost is a big factor.
[00:22] Luis: and we have existing on-prem GPU infra, plus some AWS capacity, so curious about dedicated vs hosted.
[00:28] Aisha: product is mostly about accuracy on clinical extraction, so we care about model quality and hallucination behavior.
[00:35] Jordan: great, good context. i'll start in the Console - model catalog page. (screen sharing) you'll see we have curated open models and redwood-verified performance profiles. you can filter by architecture, tokenization, quantization support, and recommended sequence length.
[01:05] Ravi: quick note, the compatibility matrix is basically a csv that maps models to supported runtimes, quantization flags (8-bit, 4-bit), kernels we tested, and any ops that require fallback. helps to decide if a model will run on your Dedicated pool or needs a hosted variant.
[01:28] Samantha: can you show an example? like lLaMa-2-70b or mistral? names are always a bit fuzzy in transcripts :)
[01:35] Jordan: yeah so here we have entries for Llama-2-70b, Mistral-7b, and some community fine-tuned variants. note the perf profile for Llama-2-70b on A100 80GB: 120ms p50 for 64-token seq with batching of 8 - that's from our internal bench. on cheaper hardware or quantized 4-bit runs it's different.
[02:10] Ravi: and important to call out KV cache behavior — if you have long chat sessions the KV cache memory growth affects throughput; our runtime supports async kv eviction and prefix caching to keep p99s bounded.
[02:35] Luis: ok on the numbers, how do you measure cost? is it tokens/sec or GPU seconds?
[02:41] Jordan: we present both. the Console shows tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens, and an estimated cost-per-call based on your prompt/response lengths. Optimize will recommend batching and quantization to hit cost targets.
[03:00] Aisha: can we pin a model for a route? we want to ensure prod uses a specific ver.
[03:05] Ravi: yep, rollout configs support pinning by model version, canary percent, and automatic fallback to a compatible model family if a node fails.
[03:18] Samantha: security - do you support VPC private plane and KMS? also SOC2 compliance?
[03:25] Jordan: yes, for Private deployments we have a customer-managed control plane (VPC) and KMS + HSM integrations are supported. Redwood is SOC 2 Type II certified and we can provide the report under NDA. SSO/SAML and RBAC are available in the Console.
[03:42] Luis: good. for PII retention and logs, can we configure no-persistence?
[03:47] Ravi: yes you can set retention policies per route and disable request logging; audit logs can be redirected to your SIEM.
[03:54] Jordan: back to model selection - i'll show the compatibility matrix CSV, it lists runtime (torch/onnx/ts), quant flags, recommended kernels. for example Mistral-7b can be run quantized on T4 with ~1.5x throughput improvement but if you need certain ops we will fallback to a slower kernel.
[04:25] Samantha: do you have benchmark artifacts we can run ourselves?
[04:29] Jordan: we typically share a bench spreadsheet and a POC harness. ravi will run a POC with your prompts to reproduce numbers on your infra.
[04:36] Ravi: for the POC I'd like your typical prompt distribution — short Q/A vs long clinical narratives — and target seq lengths; that will determine batching and kv strategies.
[04:46] Luis: we can share that. curious about streaming vs non-streaming latencies for user-facing chat.
[04:52] Ravi: streaming adds a tiny bit of overhead but perceived latency is much better. our streaming path uses a different kernel pipeline to flush tokens early; p50 is usually similar but p90/p99 can improve because you get partial tokens sooner.
[05:15] Aisha: coherence on hallucinations — do you have evals tied to prompt sets?
[05:20] Jordan: yes Optimize includes quality monitoring; we tie regression alerts to evaluation prompt sets so if a new model or quant profile increases hallucination rate we flag it. we can run those evals with your prompts during POC.
[05:36] Samantha: ok on Dedicated vs Hosted — if we go dedicated what's the commitment and scaling model?
[05:43] Jordan: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with commit tiers monthly/annual. you get predictable throughput and data isolation. autoscaling policies and burst capacity can be configured. for private on-prem we'd discuss the on-prem package and support SLA.
[05:59] Luis: and how about cost tradeoffs for 8-bit vs 4-bit quant?
[06:04] Ravi: 8-bit usually gives 1.5-2x perf improvement with minimal quality loss; 4-bit can be more aggressive and sometimes needs finetuning or special kernels. our compatibility matrix flags models that are well-behaved at 4-bit.
[06:20] Samantha: competitors question — we looked at AWS Bedrock and Anthropic. why pick Redwood?
[06:27] Jordan: two things—first, production-first observability and cost tooling (Console + Optimize) gives you unit economics visibility. second, unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private so you can move without re-architecting. also our compatibility matrix reduces surprises when porting models.
[06:48] Luis: can we run a quick sanity check - show pinning and model rollouts in Console?
[06:52] Jordan: sure — (screen) route config, pick model, set canary 10% -> we also show fallback policy to Mistral-7b if Llama-2-70b can't be loaded.
[07:10] Ravi: small note: some model names may be transcribed wrong in the csv, but the Console uses canonical model ids.
[07:20] Samantha: thanks, that helps. about benchmarks: will you run on our on-prem nodes or do you need us to open access?
[07:28] Ravi: ideally we run within your environment — we can provide the POC harness container and runbench scripts. if networking is an issue we can do a joint run where you share anonymized logs.
[07:40] Aisha: timeline — we want a short POC within two weeks. possible?
[07:44] Jordan: yes, we can target a 2-week POC; ravi will send proposed dates.
[07:49] Luis: any gotchas with the model catalog when using custom finetuned models?
[07:53] Ravi: custom finetunes are supported but we recommend running through the compatibility checks; some finetuned ops may require fallback kernels. we put notes in the matrix per-model.
[08:08] Samantha: ok last question - can Optimize recommend quant profiles automatically based on prompt set?
[08:13] Jordan: yes Optimize analyzes prompt distribution and suggests batching, quantization profiles and cost estimates. it will also simulate expected latency and p99s.
[08:25] Ravi: and we'll attach those recommendations to the POC report so you can decide tradeoffs.
[08:32] Jordan: quick recap: we'll share the compatibility matrix and benchmark sheet, ravi will propose POC dates and runbench plan, maplehealth to share prompt sets and throughput targets.
[08:46] Samantha: that works. thanks everyone.
[08:50] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and files. bye.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcribed model names and acronyms, speaker overlaps, and some punctuation issues. The body includes natural pauses, filler words, and interruptions as seen above.

End of transcript.
